audit.whatIsWrong: The last three chart rows are all 'Skill' while their own whys[] say otherwise: whys[4] 'Level 6 stays dangerous', whys[5] 'First item favours you', whys[6] 'At 2+ items you out-scale'.
audit.why: The packet chart is [Sylas x5, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo] and agrees with the whys[] on all seven rows. The shape is right: Sylas owns lane through 6 because Hijack turns your own ultimate on you, and the flip lands on your first tank item.
audit.corrected: L1-L6 Sylas, first item Dr. Mundo, 2+ items Dr. Mundo.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is described as your Maximum Dosage spike. It is the opposite, and Hijack's cooldown never appears anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30 and Maximum Dosage is 120. At rank 1 he can steal and use your ultimate, then have Hijack back 40 seconds before you have yours. That single number is the whole level-6 rule: whoever presses R second wins, and it is never you unless you wait.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why, mid, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now carry 80s against 120s and the 'never ult first' rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields describe Kingslayer as percent-health or percent-missing-health damage, and wants.you[1] tells the reader to stack HP so that damage 'falls off'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Kingslayer is 'Sylas lunges at an enemy with magical force dealing damage and healing himself against enemy champions' — a 400-range lunge that damages and heals. Nothing in it scales off your health bar. The advice built on top of it is worse than the error: if a spell did scale on your health, stacking health would make it hit harder, not softer. The correct counter to Kingslayer is Grievous Wounds, which is exactly what the supplied needs-antiheal interaction says and what report[8].t's item build already supports.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, spikes[2].text, early, late and wants.you[1] now describe Kingslayer as damage-plus-heal answered by Grievous Wounds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Only one cooldown appeared, and the sequencing cue count in the packet is 6 — the highest in this slice — yet none of it was tied to a number.
audit.why: Abscond/Abduct 13/12/11/10/9 at 400 range, Kingslayer 12/10.5/9/7.5/6, Chain Lash 10/9/8/7/6 at 775, Hijack 80/55/30. Chain Lash outranges nothing you have — Infected Bonesaw is 975 — so the poke war is winnable; it is the dash that beats you.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now lists three of them with the rank-1 values and what each one means for your step-up.

audit.why: Chain Lash reaches 775 and Infected Bonesaw reaches 975, so the trade rule the page already implies — poke from range, never brawl inside his dash — holds. What was missing was the number, now in spikes[0].text and early.

edits.before: Maximum Dosage online — dives and all-ins flip when you press R mid-fight and regen half your HP. Force Sylas to commit, then out-last the commit.
edits.after: His window: Hijack is 80s at rank 1 against your 120s, so he steals Maximum Dosage and gets it back before you do. Do not ult first here.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct (13s): matchup-defining — His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct (13s at rank 1, 400 range): matchup-defining — bait the dash, then commit while it is down. - Kingslayer (12s at rank 1) heals him off you: Grievous Wounds is the answer, not more health. - Hijack (80s at rank 1) steals your 120s ultimate, so never ult first.

edits.before: Track Sylas’s Abscond / Abduct (13s): His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Hijack (80s at rank 1) takes your 120s Maximum Dosage — it is back before yours is. Kingslayer heals him: bring Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: Sylas owns this window: his E Abscond/Abduct chain gives him mobility to dodge your Q Infected Bonesaw, his W Kingslayer heals off you and does %-missing-HP damage, and his Q chains poke you down while you can't pin him — expect to lose the early trades and eat sustain.
edits.after: Sylas owns this window: Abscond (E, 13s) dashes him off your Bonesaw and recasts to chain back in, Kingslayer (W, 12s at rank 1) damages you and heals him for it, and Chain Lash pokes from 775 while you cannot pin him. Expect to lose these trades and farm.

edits.before: Your spike arrives here: once you have a tank item your HP pool blunts his %-HP Kingslayer, your Q slow finally catches his E dashes on cooldown, and Heart Zapper out-DPS his poke, letting you walk him down when his mobility is down.
edits.after: Your spike arrives here: a tank item plus Grievous Wounds cuts the Kingslayer heal that carried him, your Q slow finally catches his E dashes on their 13s cooldown, and Heart Zapper out-DPSes his poke — walk him down while the dash is spent.

edits.before: Levels 1-5 clearly favour Sylas: his E dash-chain dodges your Q, his W Kingslayer heals off your bar with %-missing-HP damage, and his Q pokes you out while you can't pin his mobility, so you concede the early lane and farm safe.
edits.after: Levels 1-5 clearly favour Sylas: Abscond dashes off your Q and recasts to chain back, Kingslayer heals him for the damage he does to you, and Chain Lash pokes from 775 while you cannot pin his mobility. Concede the lane and farm safe.

edits.before: Level 6 stays dangerous because Hijack lets him steal Maximum Dosage and turn your own sustain into his all-in engine — don't feed him a losing fight where he gets your ult plus Kingslayer.
edits.after: Level 6 stays dangerous: Hijack is 80s at rank 1 against your 120s, so he steals Maximum Dosage and has it back before you do. Never press R first — cast it only once his is spent.

edits.before: Your first tank item flips it: HP blunts his %-HP burst, Q slow catches his dashes on cooldown, and R heals through his combo, so from items onward you out-scale and walk him down whenever his mobility is spent.
edits.after: Your first tank item flips it: Grievous Wounds kills the Kingslayer heal, Q slow catches his dashes on cooldown, and R heals through his combo, so from items onward you out-scale and walk him down whenever the dash is spent.

edits.before: Stack HP so his W Kingslayer %-HP damage and heal fall off
edits.after: Bring Grievous Wounds so W Kingslayer stops healing him

notes:
The biggest fix here is not the chart, it is that five fields called Kingslayer a percent-health spell and then told the reader to stack health against it. Riot's text has no health scaling in Kingslayer at all, and if it did, stacking health would make it worse. The counter is Grievous Wounds, which the item section already builds toward.

Second: Hijack's cooldown was nowhere on a page whose whole level-6 section is about Hijack. 80s at rank 1 against Maximum Dosage's 120s is the concrete rule the packet's six sequencing cues were asking for.

UNVERIFIED, left alone: breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t described Abscond/Abduct as 'dash + stun (recast pull)'. Riot's text says only 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits' — no stun, and the pull moves Sylas rather than the target. The kit's derived flags for E list projectile and dash but no hardCC. I could not confirm from source whether Abduct applies a stun, so I did not assert either way, and I therefore did NOT write the obvious follow-on claim that Mundo's passive resists it. If someone can confirm the stun, that interaction belongs on this page.
